paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption_used: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline MistralV0.2-Base and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. The chart displays six specialty groups along the x-axis (Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, Pediatrics), with the y-axis showing negative log probability ranging from approximately -27 to -22. Within each group, the MistralV0.2-Base bar (light blue) consistently shows the highest negative log probability, indicating weaker token predictions at baseline. Among the fine-tuned models, the Gastro-tuned variant achieves the lowest negative log probability across most specialty groups, suggesting strong cross-specialty transfer. Notably, the Infect group shows the largest overall bar heights, with baseline reaching approximately -23.5, while the Cardio group exhibits the smallest spread between baseline and fine-tuned variants at roughly 1.5 units.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log probability for clinically relevant tokens when comparing a baseline MistralV0.2-Base model with models fine-tuned on various clinical specialties. The horizontal axis represents six clinical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics, ordered from left to right. The vertical axis displays negative log probability, ranging from approximately -27 to -22, and utilizes a linear scale with tick intervals of approximately 1.5 units. The MistralV0.2-Base model is represented by light blue bars, each approximately -25.5 units in height, while the fine-tuned models are represented by orange bars. The Gastro-tuned model consistently exhibits the lowest negative log probability among the fine-tuned models, with bar heights ranging from approximately -23.5 to -23. The Infect group has the tallest bar, reaching approximately -23.5, and the Cardio group displays the smallest variation in height between the baseline and fine-tuned models, with a difference of approximately 1.5 units.
